procedure_metadata.title: Flatten AI-NLEP Meta-Procedure Into Canonical Atomic JSON Projection
procedure_metadata.purpose: Retrieve the canonical AI-NLEP meta-procedure and deterministically decompose it into the canonical atomic JSON flattening representation defined by the GeminiSupervisor README.

flattening_authority.section: Canonical JSON flattening and shuffle representation

definitions.source_json: The complete parsed JSON value of 731942_ai_nlep_meta_procedure.json.
definitions.atom: One top-level projection-array element that contributes exactly one payload fact while retaining sufficient ancestor structure to identify where that fact belongs.
definitions.terminal_property: An object property whose value is not an object and not an array.
definitions.keyed_object_property: An object property whose value is an object.
definitions.keyed_array_property: An object property whose value is an array.
definitions.object_literal_atom: An atom containing a keyed empty object at the complete ancestor route to establish that the keyed property's value is an object.
definitions.array_literal_atom: An atom containing a keyed empty array at the complete ancestor route to establish that the keyed property's value is an array.
definitions.root_container_atom: The bare literal {} or [] emitted when the supplied source JSON root is respectively an object or array.
definitions.anonymous_intermediate_container: An object or array that is an array member or other unkeyed structural container whose existence and type may already be entailed by a deeper emitted atom.
definitions.payload_fact: Exactly one terminal key-value fact, keyed container-type fact, root-container-type fact, or otherwise-disappearing empty anonymous-container fact.
definitions.projection: The ordered top-level array containing all atomic JSON elements produced by this procedure.
definitions.ancestor_route: The nested source structure from the root to the atom's payload fact, preserved using the source's literal keys and required container structure.
definitions.canonical_order: The deterministic order produced by traversing the source JSON in its original object-property and array-member order.
definitions.original_array_order_authority: The original source JSON, retained by source reference and used when array order must be reconstructed after any later shuffle.

requirements: Parse the complete file as JSON.
Do not substitute an uploaded shadow copy, prior excerpt, remembered content, summary, or reconstructed equivalent when the Library source is available.
Apply the documented canonical atomic decomposition semantics literally.
Do not replace them with generic JSON flattening conventions such as dotted paths, JSON Pointer, JSONPath, row tables, key-value tuples, or path-value pairs.

instructions.primary_instruction: Retrieve the complete canonical meta-procedure JSON and transform it into a deterministic ordered array of atomic nested JSON projection elements using the canonical GeminiSupervisor flattening semantics.

operations.completion_condition: The complete Library file has been retrieved and parsed as one JSON value.
An empty projection array exists and the source root type is known.
If the root is an object, {} has been emitted exactly once; if the root is an array, [] has been emitted exactly once; otherwise no root-container atom is emitted.

inputs: each object encountered in source traversal
preconditions: The object's ancestor route is known.
operations.completion_condition: Every object property has been processed according to its value type and no two object sibling payload facts have been bundled into one atom.

preconditions: The property's value is an object.
operations.completion_condition: One atom establishes the keyed property as an object by placing the literal source key with value {} at the complete ancestor route before descendant atoms are emitted.

preconditions: The property's value is neither object nor array.
operations.completion_condition: Exactly one atom contains the terminal key and its exact source value at the complete ancestor route.

outputs: one atomic decomposition branch per array member
preconditions: The property's value is an array.
operations.completion_condition: The keyed property has one [] container atom and every array member has been independently decomposed without bundling multiple members into one payload atom.

outputs: one or more atoms attributable to exactly that member
operations.completion_condition: At the array boundary, every content atom represents exactly one source member; descendants may preserve ancestor containers required to locate its facts.

inputs: anonymous object or array encountered during recursive decomposition
outputs: no standalone atom when its existence and type are already entailed by deeper atoms
one standalone empty-container atom when the container is empty and would otherwise disappear
preconditions: The container has no literal source key at its immediate boundary.
operations.completion_condition: No redundant anonymous structural atom remains, and every empty anonymous container that would otherwise be lost is preserved.
All original keys and terminal values are preserved exactly and provenance is represented only by retained nested JSON structure rather than added generic path or index metadata.
Atoms occur in deterministic source traversal order and no shuffle has been applied.
Each atom contributes exactly one payload fact; object siblings are not bundled; multiple array members are not bundled.
Root, keyed object, keyed array, and otherwise-disappearing empty anonymous containers are represented exactly as required, with no redundant anonymous intermediate atoms.
Every source terminal property and every source array member is represented by the required atomic projection semantics with no omission or unauthorized duplication.
Recursive merging of atoms at matching nesting signatures, using canonical source order for arrays, produces a JSON value structurally and value-wise identical to source_json.

operations.object: reconstructed JSON against canonical source JSON
operations.completion_condition: The reconstructed JSON and source JSON contain identical object keys, container types, array membership and ordering, terminal values, and complete nested structure.
The projection is valid JSON and is minified without changing its structure or values.
The return object conforms to return_schema and reports complete only when all required validation checks pass.

recursive_decomposition_rules.rule: Emit {} once, then recursively process each property in canonical source order.
Emit [] once, then recursively decompose each member independently in canonical source order.
Emit the keyed {} atom at the current ancestor route, then recursively process its properties.
Emit the keyed [] atom at the current ancestor route, then independently decompose each member.
Emit exactly one atom containing the literal key and literal value at the complete ancestor route.
Do not emit a standalone structural atom when descendant atoms already establish its existence and type.
Emit the empty object member because otherwise that source fact would disappear.
Emit the empty array member because otherwise that source fact would disappear.
Emit an atom containing exactly that one member at the array boundary with all required ancestors.

required: The output projection must be 100% valid JSON.
Every top-level projection element must contribute exactly one payload fact.
All source keys must remain literal and unchanged.
All terminal source values must remain literal and unchanged.
Ancestor objects and arrays may appear inside an atom only as required to preserve the route to its one payload fact.
Every keyed object-valued property must have its own keyed {} atom before descendant atoms.
Every keyed array-valued property must have its own keyed [] atom before member atoms.
Each array member must be independently decomposed.
An empty anonymous container that would otherwise disappear must be retained.
The deterministic projection must be constructed before any optional future shuffle.
prohibited: Do not flatten into dotted paths.
Do not flatten into JSON Pointer strings.
Do not flatten into JSONPath expressions.
Do not emit generic path arrays.
Do not add array-index metadata to projection atoms.
Do not add separate provenance fields to projection atoms.
Do not bundle sibling object properties into one payload atom.
Do not bundle multiple array members into one payload atom.
Do not emit redundant anonymous intermediate container atoms when descendants already establish the container's existence and type.
Do not shuffle raw keys, scalar values, nested atom content, characters, or internal object structure.
Do not use a preexisting flattened artifact as evidence that this procedure was executed.

invariants.statement: Every emitted atom adds exactly one payload fact.
Every terminal source property appears exactly once as a terminal payload fact.
Every keyed object or keyed array container fact appears exactly once as its corresponding empty-container atom.
No atom contains payload facts from two sibling object properties.
No atom contains more than one member at any decomposed array boundary.
Nested structure inside an atom represents provenance through original JSON structure rather than auxiliary path metadata.
The source JSON can be reconstructed losslessly when the projection is combined with the source's original array ordering.

checks.pass_condition: The complete Library JSON parses successfully.
Every projection element contributes exactly one payload fact.
Every terminal property from source_json maps to exactly one terminal atom.
All required root, keyed, and otherwise-disappearing empty containers are represented.
No projection atom contains synthetic provenance keys, generic path fields, or array-index metadata.
Each atom contains only the ancestor structure plus one payload fact.
At each decomposed array boundary, a content atom contains exactly one source member.
Reconstruction from projection plus original array order is structurally and value-wise identical to source_json.
The final projection parses as valid JSON after minification.

verification_model.completion_rule: Status may be complete only if V1-V9 all pass in the current execution.

complete_when: The returned projection is the projection constructed during the current execution.
incomplete_when: Flattening or validation work remains and can still be performed.
blocked_when: The canonical Library source cannot be retrieved or parsed.
The governing flattening specification cannot be established.
Lossless reconstruction cannot be achieved without inventing semantics not authorized by the canonical procedure.
must_not_claim_complete_when: Any source portion was not processed.
Any validation check is unevaluated or failed.
Completion is inferred from a preexisting flattened artifact.
The returned projection was not produced by the current execution.

return_contract.omission_policy: No field required by the return_schema may be omitted. A complete status requires populated execution and validation evidence.
return_contract.extension_policy: Additional diagnostic fields may be added only when they do not alter the projection semantics or substitute for required fields.

original_order.rule: Use original source array order when reconstruction requires sequence.
